title: Integral generators of $D^b_c(X,E)$ and $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$
statement:
Let $X$ be a standing scheme and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite. Let $\mathcal G_E$ be the class of
objects $(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]=E_X\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}a_!L_0$ of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$, where
$a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ is a locally closed immersion and $L_0$ a lisse finite free
$\cO_{E,S}$-module (locally on $S$), and $\mathcal G_{\Qlb}$ the class of
$\QbarX\otimes_{\cO_{E,X}}a_!L_0$ for all finite $E$ and such $a$, $L_0$.

1. Every object of $\Dbc(X,E)$ is obtained from $\mathcal G_E$ by finitely many cones and shifts.
2. Every object of $\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is obtained from $\mathcal G_{\Qlb}$ by finitely many cones and
   shifts (with one finite $E$ for the given object).
3. $a_!L_0\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, and its reductions $a_!L_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}\cO_E/\pi_E^n=a_!(L_0/\pi_E^n)$
   lie in $\Dbc(X,\cO_E/\pi_E^n)$ and come from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X Noetherian. Coefficient-heart generation expresses every bounded constructible finite-extension object by a finite cone-and-shift construction from degree-zero locally closed extensions of lisse sheaves.

source.place: (1): Noetherianity and reduction to the heart

proof.text: Identify the spectral-norm coefficients of the lattice-subquotient theorem with the specified finite field and its integers, using ULift and equality of the spectral and given norms. Transport its filtration along these ring isomorphisms. Each successive quotient is a specified integral generator. Its short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle, so finite filtration induction and then induction over the heart cone construction prove (1).

Descend an algebraic-closure object to one finite E. The scalar-extension functor is exact, so its left-derived functor agrees with its termwise derived functor and preserves shifts and triangles. It sends each finite-extension generator to exactly the specified algebraic-closure generator. Transport the finite-extension construction and its final isomorphism to obtain (2), with the same E throughout.

For (3), local freeness gives finite constant local models. Apply the generic stratified open-extension and closed-pushforward arguments from the lisse-extension constructibility proof to the integral module. Their degree-zero complex is bounded constructible. The same argument applies after any ordinary coefficient extension, which preserves local freeness via its regular-module isomorphism.

Tensor commutes with normalized inverse image. Flatness is detected on a closed subscheme and its complementary open by vanishing of the kernel of every tensor image of a monomorphism. The unit, counit and off-support zero identities imply that both open extension and closed pushforward preserve flatness. Thus the integral extension is flat, its single complex is K-flat, and its left-derived scalar extension is its ordinary scalar extension. Ordinary scalar extension commutes with open extension and with closed pushforward, by the same support identities; this gives the specified reduction isomorphism.

Each residue ring is finite by the proved finite-quotient theorem for the ring of integers, since the given uniformizer generates its maximal ideal. Its uniformizer-power ideal contains an open norm ball, so the quotient topology is discrete. Finite discrete constructible encoding gives constructibility of the underlying sheaf. The explicit fixed-scalar realization has this same underlying sheaf; finite local constancy and finite stratifications transfer across that isomorphism. Its underlying abelian-sheaf functor is exact and conservative, hence the realization is exact. Derived homology comparison therefore preserves constructible cohomology and bounds. The finite-ring constructible derived-origin theorem supplies exactly the etale essential-image assertion required in (3).

source.place: (3): finite fixed-scalar realization and etale origin

proof_origin.place: Proof (1)-(3), formalized by W4: retain lattice filtration, finite cone generation and descent; prove the single reduction using flatness and support, and use finite-ring derived origin after the explicit fixed-scalar realization.
